author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, shown by full name. All specialties render on one page and nothing links to it.
acceptance_criteria: opening GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, each under its stored name
each specialty lists the veterinarians holding it, shown as first name then last name, for example "Helen Leary"
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
every specialty renders on the one page, with no paging
a specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it
a veterinarian holding more than one specialty appears under each of them
specialties, and the veterinarians within each, appear in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one
a clinic that knows no specialties yields a page that renders and lists none
no navigation item and no page link leads to the specialty directory
every piece of the page's wording is present in each supported language, per REQ-LANG-002
non_goals: managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application — NG-2 is unchanged by this slice
a navigation item or a link from another page leading to the specialty directory; the owner named a visible entry point as a possible follow-up request
searching or filtering the specialty directory (NG-9)
notes: REQ-SYS-001 still binds: the page carries the site's existing navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory like every other page. Out of scope is only a link pointing at this page. Two questions stayed open under the dispatch's no-further-answers constraint and are recorded in the PRD Open Questions: whether the page gets a visible entry point, and which sort order applies (only stability is decided). Narrow readings taken where the request was silent: an unheld specialty still appears because the request says every specialty; the empty-clinic case renders rather than fails.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is a second read-only projection of vet-package data and stays inside the vet feature package (system-design.md Package Structure). It reuses the in-force patterns unchanged: Spring Data repository read directly by a web controller, Thymeleaf page composed through fragments/layout, message keys in every bundle. One adjustment is needed, and it is why this is not 'covered': VetRepository cannot satisfy the criterion 'a specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed', because it reads vets only. A SpecialtyRepository is added for the Specialty lookup value, mirroring owner/PetTypeRepository exactly (JpaRepository plus one explicit ORDER BY name query). The join of specialties to the vets holding them is assembled by a pure static factory on a new package-private value object in the vet package, so the grouping and ordering stay unit-testable without a Spring context and the controller keeps only bind-delegate-select. No new pattern, module, dependency, or ADR.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html is a third route on VetController, alongside /vets.html and /vets; the prd-entry file_targets already name VetController, and the directory reads the same vet plus specialty data, so no SpecialtyController is introduced
VetController gains a second constructor argument, SpecialtyRepository; VetControllerTests must declare a matching test double or the @WebMvcTest context fails to start

the controller reads specialties from SpecialtyRepository (name order) and vets from the existing VetRepository.findAll(), which is @Cacheable("vets") and eagerly fetches specialties, so no session is needed at render time
the assembly is a pure static factory taking the two collections and returning the ordered listings; the controller adds the result under one model attribute and returns the view name

specialtyList.html renders through ~{fragments/layout :: layout (~{::body},'specialties')}, satisfying REQ-SYS-001; the menu argument matches no navbar item, so nothing is highlighted and no navigation entry is added
the new template and any new message keys are checked by I18nPropertiesSyncTest, which fails on literal text between tags and on any base key missing from a locale bundle

patterns.description: lookup-value repository with an explicit ORDER BY name query; SpecialtyRepository is the same shape for Specialty. Specialty is a lookup value rather than an aggregate root, and this slice is read-only (NG-2 unchanged), so the Repository row's one-per-root rule is not stretched by a read gateway
existing precedent for a vet-package type that exists only to shape output; the new listing type is its render-side counterpart, but immutable and equal by value per the in-force Value object row
addPaginationModel: the existing in-controller model-assembly shape the new handler follows
layout fragment invocation, table markup, and #{} key usage to copy

risks.risk: grouping vets to specialties by object identity or by equals: BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, and the two repository calls run in separate persistence contexts, so the Specialty instances reachable from a Vet are not the instances SpecialtyRepository returns
risks.mitigation: group by specialty id, never by instance identity or by name; the specialties table has a non-unique name index, so name is not a safe key

risks.risk: stable order (acceptance criterion 7) is left open by the PRD, so an arbitrary iteration order could ship and pass a weak test
risks.mitigation: narrowest reading consistent with the codebase: specialties by stored name via the repository query, matching PetTypeRepository and Vet.getSpecialties(); veterinarians by last name, then first name, then id, so the order is total even for two vets sharing a name

risks.risk: annotating the new specialty query @Cacheable would reference a cache CacheConfiguration does not declare, and unsettled vet-cache invalidation is already Open Question 5 in system-design.md
risks.mitigation: do not cache the specialty read; this slice adds no cache and no CacheConfiguration change

risks.risk: reusing an existing message key whose translated wording carries a different sentence role produces a wrong translation in inflected locales, which the key-sync test cannot detect
risks.mitigation: reuse vets, name, specialties, and none only as plain labels; add a distinct key wherever the wording states something new, and add every new key to messages.properties and to all nine translated bundles (the sync test skips messages_en.properties by design)

risks.risk: the page reads every specialty and every vet unbounded on each request
risks.mitigation: accepted: no paging is an explicit requirement, the dataset is a fixed seed of three specialties and six vets, and the vet read is served from the existing cache

notes: Trust boundary: the new route accepts no path variable, no query parameter, and no body, so it deliberately has less input surface than /vets.html, which parses a page parameter. The only boundary crossed is vet and specialty names rendered into HTML, where Thymeleaf's default escaping applies and is not disabled. No new control is required and none is invented. Divergence from the prd-entry file_targets, recorded for audit: SpecialtyRepository.java and the listing value object are added because VetRepository alone cannot list an unheld specialty, and VetRepository itself needs no change. Test placement guidance, not a mandate: six of the eight named behaviors (unheld specialty, multi-specialty vet, vet with no specialty, one page, stable order, empty clinic) are properties of the pure assembly function and are best driven by a plain JUnit test with real Vet and Specialty objects, per the testing brief's preference for real objects over mocks; the route, view name, and rendered-content assertions belong in VetControllerTests with MockMvc, and following that file's existing @MockitoBean shape there is the consistent choice. No edit to docs/system-design.md: it records current state, and these are new instances of catalogued patterns rather than a pattern change. After the slice lands, doc-sync adds a Contracts row for SpecialtyRepository and the listing type, adds REQ-VET-003 to the Implements cells for VetController, VetRepository, and Specialty, and extends the VetController Purpose text. 'Specialty directory' is the PRD's name for this page and is not yet a term in docs/ubiquitous-language.md; whether it becomes vocabulary is the product-requirements-expert's call, not a blocker here.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyListing and SpecialtyRepository follow the naming rules in docs/architecture-principles.md (no prohibited suffixes, domain-noun value object)

SpecialtyListing.directoryOf is a pure static factory with a well-documented, deliberate id-based matching strategy (Javadoc explains why identity/name matching would be wrong), matching the design-block's stated risk mitigation
Comparators (BY_STORED_NAME, BY_VETERINARIAN_NAME) give the directory a total, stable order as required by the PRD, with clear Javadoc explaining the tie-break rationale
SpecialtyListing is an immutable record with a defensive List.copyOf in its compact constructor
VetController.showSpecialtyDirectory follows the existing bind-delegate-select shape and constructor injection, consistent with the rest of the controller
SpecialtyRepository mirrors PetTypeRepository's lookup-repository shape (JpaRepository + explicit ORDER BY query) as the design-block specified

specialtyList.html follows vetList.html's layout-fragment and table conventions; message keys are correctly reused (vets) or newly added and applied consistently across messages.properties and all nine translated bundles
No mutable state, no null returns (empty lists instead), no swallowed exceptions, no logging concerns applicable to this pure, read-only slice

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No injection surface added: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a static JPQL string with no parameters and no concatenation, matching PetTypeRepository:36; the handler takes no path variable, query parameter, or body, so GET /specialties.html has strictly less request-derived input than /vets.html.

Output escaping intact: specialtyList.html renders every dynamic value through th:text (listing.name, the vet full-name expression) and message keys through #{}; no th:utext, th:inline, or other escaping bypass appears anywhere under src/main/resources/templates. Thymeleaf default escaping stays on, per security-principles.md Cross-site scripting row.

No new exposure beyond the recorded baseline: the page discloses veterinarian first and last names and specialty names, exactly the data already served unauthenticated by the existing /vets.html page and the /vets JSON route. The absence of authentication is the demonstration's recorded posture (system-design.md Security Context) and is explicitly not a finding; the change does not leave the application weaker than that baseline. The endpoint and what it exposes are stated in prd.md REQ-VET-003 and in the design-block trust-boundary note.

No mass-assignment surface: the handler is read-only, binds nothing, and adds no WebDataBinder, so the identifier-disallow rule has nothing to apply to. No file, classpath, or resource path is composed from caller input; the view name is a literal.

No secrets introduced: a search of the new Java sources, the new template, and the message bundles for credential-shaped names (token, password, secret, apikey) returns nothing; the ten bundle additions are three display labels each.
No serialization or deserialization entry point added; SpecialtyListing is an immutable record assembled server-side and never bound from a request.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle, the Gradle wrapper, and settings.gradle are absent from the change set (git status confirms), so no dependency, repository, or checksum surface moved and the four dependency checks have nothing to clear.
No error path added that could carry internal detail outward: the handler has no exception handling and produces no message from data-store state.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() carries a custom JPQL query (`SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name`) that is exercised in the test suite only through a Mockito stub in VetControllerTests — no test runs it against a real database. The project's established seam for exactly this (ClinicServiceTests, @DataJpaTest, e.g. shouldFindVets against VetRepository.findAll()) is untouched by this slice. A typo'd JPQL property, a wrong ORDER BY direction, or a broken mapping would pass every test in this change set and still break at runtime — jacoco shows the repository interface at 100% only because a declarative Spring Data interface has no bytecode to instrument, which is exactly the gap testing-principles.md flags: coverage is judged by behavior exercised, not lines touched.
findings.fix: Add a @DataJpaTest-backed test to ClinicServiceTests (or a same-shape SpecialtyRepository test) that calls specialties.findSpecialties() against the real seeded H2 test database and asserts the returned specialties are present and ordered by name.

findings.description: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyOnOnePage calls the fully-qualified java.util.stream.IntStream.rangeClosed(...) even though IntStream is already imported at the top of the file (line 19) — inconsistent with the rest of the file's style.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyListing.directoryOf has 8 dedicated plain-JUnit unit tests built on real Vet/Specialty objects (no mocks), matching the brief's mocking policy and correctly placing the assembly logic at the base of the pyramid while VetControllerTests stays a thin wiring check — exactly the shape testing-principles.md's 'ratio moves when logic moves' calls for

The two acceptance criteria most likely to hide behind seed data are both directly tested: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyNoVeterinarianHolds (a specialty with zero holders still appears) and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansBySpecialtyIdRatherThanName (two same-named specialties with different ids are kept separate and a holder is attributed by id, not name or instance identity)
All four prd.md edge cases for REQ-VET-003 have dedicated tests: no-holder specialty, multi-specialty veterinarian, stable ordering (by name/id then last/first/id), and an empty specialty list

Test data construction goes through factory methods (specialty(id,name), vet(id,first,last,held...)) with SOME_ID marking the one irrelevant value and no bare mystery literals in assertions; test names follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school
Four-phase structure (arrange/act/assert separated by blank lines, no phase comments) is followed throughout both test classes
jacoco reports 100% instruction and line coverage for VetController and SpecialtyListing, clearing the brief's 80% domain-package target

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Eighteen files look wide but nine of them are translation bundles gaining the same three appended keys; the only edit to existing production code is VetController taking a second constructor argument and a new handler, and everything else is new files inside the vet feature package. No sensitive path, no build, schema, dependency or configuration change, and no existing route, query or template is altered.

semantic_surprise.note: Every hunk reads as its description promises. The one non-obvious choice, matching veterinarians to specialties by id rather than by name or instance identity, is deliberate, documented in the Javadoc, and pinned by a test with two same-named specialties; the layout fragment is invoked with a menu argument that matches no navbar item, which I confirmed against fragments/layout.html yields no navigation entry and no highlight; Vet.specialties is EAGER, so assembling outside a session is safe; all dynamic values render through th:text with default escaping. The only latent sharp edge is Objects.equals on ids treating two null-id entities as the same specialty, which the controller path cannot reach because both collections come from the database.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes at each layer rather than restating the implementation: eight plain-JUnit tests on the pure factory using real Vet and Specialty objects cover no-holder specialties, multi-specialty veterinarians, total ordering and the same-name-different-id case; the MockMvc test renders actual HTML and asserts Helen Leary appears while the unspecialized James Carter does not, which is the omission rule and the first-then-last name order at once; and a real DataJpaTest exercises the JPQL against seeded H2, closing the gap the test-reviewer flagged. The only line no assertion covers is the cosmetic no-veterinarians placeholder, which no acceptance criterion names.

reviewer_hedging.note: The first pass ran the full battery: security and doc approved with empty findings lists, and code-quality and test raised only fixable autofix items, an unused-import style call and the missing real-database test. Both were fixed and both reviewers re-approved with empty findings. The fix pass dispatched only code-quality and test, so the silence of security and doc in that pass is the scoped review plan working as designed, not a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, zero consultations and zero build retries; the design-block cleared the slice as minor and the delivered file set matches its primary paths, with ClinicServiceTests added only because a reviewer asked for it. The PRD edit is the slice's own requirement entry, and its incidental correction of the stale open-question count from ten to five matches the five unresolved bullets I counted in the file.

rationale: Additive read-only page confined to the vet package; the only edit to existing code is a constructor argument. Deliberate id-based matching is documented and tested, escaping and eager fetch check out, and all four reviewers approved with no residual findings. Confirm and merge.
